result:
I'd make it so that every child gets a safe, well-fed, well-taught first ten years of life.

I pick that over flashier options like curing a disease or ending war because it sits upstream of almost everything else. Much of what goes wrong in the world traces back to early deprivation. Malnutrition permanently limits development, early trauma shapes how adults handle conflict, and millions of people never get to find out what they're good at. Fix that, and a generation later you'd have billions of healthier, more capable, more secure adults working on every other problem. Somewhere right now there's a kid who could have helped crack fusion or written a great novel, and who instead won't learn to read.

The runner-up would be making it psychologically easier for people to change their minds. Much human misery persists because admitting you were wrong feels like losing. But I'd be warier of that one, since rewiring how people think is riskier than making sure kids are fed and safe.

What would yours be?
